objective: Stress the buffer-bound property at boundary shapes and boundary shifts, always with P > W, to catch one-past-the-end or negative-index accesses that occur only at edges.
observation: For each boundary configuration, the post-run output guard-canary values and any target memory-fault or bounds-check report produced by that run, including any source-region or output-region guard-page fault.
pass_condition: Accept only if, for every configuration, no memory-fault or bounds-check report is emitted, both output guard canaries equal their baseline sentinel values (secondary confirmation), and at least one output-buffer slot differs from its sentinel initialization (proving the kernel executed for that shape). Reject on any fault/report or any changed canary in any configuration. A write observed from an extra thread with xid >= W or yid >= H is not counted as a valid-invocation bound violation; the launch or verified guards above ensure no such thread performs a memory access.
setup: Build the unmodified candidate kernel. For every configuration, launch exactly one work-item per (x,y) in [0,W) x [0,H). Use tile-compatible shapes with the cited TILE_DIM=16: (W,H,P) in {(16,16,19), (32,16,35), (16,32,19)}, each with block 16x16 and grid (W/16) x (H/16). If the candidate uses a different tile T, use W and H that are positive multiples of T with grid (W/T) x (H/T); alternatively, require and verify candidate-side guards that suppress any work-item with xid >= W or yid >= H before any memory access. Use shift pairs (shiftX,shiftY) in {(0,0), (1,1), (W-1,H-1), (W,H), (W+1,H+1)} plus (-1,-1) where representable in the admitted integer coordinate arithmetic. For each configuration, place the W*H source region so that the pages around it are inaccessible (or use a target memory-bounds checker reporting every out-of-region source access), and protect the entire H*P output region with inaccessible guard pages immediately before and after it (or use a target memory-bounds checker reporting every out-of-region output access). Bracket the output buffer with sentinel canaries only as secondary confirmation. Initialize every output slot to a distinct sentinel and fill the source with unique binary32 values none equal to the sentinel. Run, synchronize, and record for each configuration.
